label: History
value: Aunt Em was a young wife.
unit: Aunt Em was a young, pretty wife when she first came to live on the Kansas prairie. She lived in a drab, gray environment with her husband Uncle Henry, her niece Dorothy, and Dorothy's dog Toto until a sudden and severe cyclone struck the farm, forcing Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. After Dorothy was carried away by the storm to the Land of Oz, Aunt Em eventually was outside watering her cabbages when Dorothy ran toward her. She joyfully embraced her niece, who expressed her happiness to be back home.

label: History
value: Bug was born as an ordinary woggle-bug.
unit: Born as an ordinary woggle-bug, the Bug spent three years living in a school-house hearth before being magnified by a professor's magnifying glass and escaping unnoticed into a nearby grove. In his wanderings, he also saved the ninth life of a tailor. He eventually encounters Tip and his companions, introducing himself as the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug and joining their travel to the Emerald City, where he suggests using a leg from Jack Pumpkinhead to repair the Saw-Horse's broken leg. During their journey, he annoys the group with puns and helps navigate magical illusions to reach the city, only to become trapped in the royal palace when General Jinjur ambushes them. After escaping the palace aboard the animated, flying Gump, the group crashes into a giant Jackdaw nest, where the Woggle-Bug finds a diamond necklace and gifts it to the Tin Woodman. When the birds attack, he is sheltered under the Scarecrow's straw, and he later successfully uses one of Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills to repair the Gump's damaged wings. He flies with the companions to Glinda the Good's palace, accompanies her forces as they capture Mombi and uncover Tip's true identity as Princess Ozma, and witnesses Ozma's final victory and coronation after an aerial assault on the Emerald City.

label: Quote
value: Bug said: "I have never ceased to congratulate myself for escaping while I was Highly Magnified; for even my excessive knowledge would have proved of little use to me had I remained a tiny, insignificant insect."

label: Quote
value: Bug said: "If the Pumpkinhead is to ride, why not use one of his legs to make a leg for the horse that carries him? I judge that both are made of wood."

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “But you were the King until she came,” said the Woggle-Bug, strutting up and down with his hands in his pockets; “so it appears to me that she is the interloper instead of you.”

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “As for me,” said the Woggle-Bug, “I think that I could live for some time on Jack Pumpkinhead. Not that I prefer pumpkins for food; but I believe they are somewhat nutritious, and Jack’s head is large and plump.”

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “You have; and I’ve restrained a good many of them,” replied the insect. “But there are opportunities for so many excellent puns in our language that, to an educated person like myself, the temptation to express them is almost irresistible.”

label: Personality
value: The Cowardly Lion considers himself a wild beast.
unit: The Cowardly Lion considers himself a wild beast who is nevertheless a coward, expressing that he is afraid of everything. His primary motivation is to seek courage from the Wizard, Oz, as he finds his life unbearable without it and hopes to genuinely become the King of Beasts as men call him. Specifically, he desires the kind of courage that allows him to forget his fears. Despite his inherent cowardice, he also views himself as content in the knowledge that he is as brave as any beast that ever lived. He harbors specific fears, including a terror of falling and a terrible fear of the Kalidahs.

label: History
value: The Cowardly Lion believed he was born a coward.
unit: Believing he was born a coward, the Cowardly Lion initially survived by roaring loudly to terrify men and other creatures into fleeing. While traveling through a forest, he attacked Dorothy's friends and threatened her dog, but after Dorothy slapped his nose and called him a coward, he admitted his secret lack of courage and joined her journey to seek help from the Great Oz. Along the path to the Emerald City, he helped carry his companions over dangerous chasms, but later fell into a deep sleep in a field of poisonous poppies until he was rescued by thousands of field mice. Upon reaching Oz's palace, the Lion encountered Oz as a Ball of Fire and was tasked with killing the Wicked Witch of the West. When the Witch sent her forces against the travelers, the Lion was captured and imprisoned, but Dorothy secretly fed him while he resisted the Witch's attempt to starve him. Following the Witch's destruction, he rejoined his friends, returned to the Emerald City, and drank a liquid potion provided by Oz, which he happily believed gave him true courage. Journeying south with Dorothy afterward, he decapitated a giant spider monster terrorizing a grand forest, earning the allegiance of the woodland creatures who proclaimed him King of the Forest. After traveling to the realm of Glinda the Good Witch, Glinda arranged to send him back to rule over the forest animals before Dorothy used her magical shoes to return home.

value: Cowardly Lion said: “If you wish,” said the Lion, “I will go into the forest and kill a deer for you. You can roast it by the fire, since your tastes are so peculiar that you prefer cooked food, and then you will have a very good breakfast.”

label: Quote
value: Cowardly Lion said: “I am terribly afraid of falling, myself,” said the Cowardly Lion, “but I suppose there is nothing to do but try it. So get on my back and we will make the attempt.”

label: Quote
value: Cowardly Lion said: “They are monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers,” replied the Lion, “and with claws so long and sharp that they could tear me in two as easily as I could kill Toto. I’m terribly afraid of the Kalidahs.”

label: Quote
value: Cowardly Lion said: "We are lost, for they will surely tear us to pieces with their sharp claws. But stand close behind me, and I will fight them as long as I am alive."

label: Quote
value: Cowardly Lion said: "I am a Cowardly Lion, afraid of everything. I came to you to beg that you give me courage, so that in reality I may become the King of Beasts, as men call me."

label: History
value: Dorothy is an orphan
unit: Dorothy, an orphan who lived with her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em on the dry gray prairies of Kansas, was swept away inside her farmhouse by a severe cyclone. She landed in the magical Land of Oz, inadvertently crushing the Wicked Witch of the East. Given the Witch's silver shoes by the Witch of the North and advised to seek help from the Great Wizard Oz, Dorothy set out along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City to find a way home. Along her journey, she befriended and recruited the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, facing numerous hazards including dangerous Kalidahs, a swift river, and a field of sleeping poppies before reaching their destination. Upon arriving at the Emerald City, the group met Oz, who demanded they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West before he would grant their wishes. Traveling to the West, they were attacked by the Witch's forces, and Dorothy was captured and enslaved in the Witch's castle. Dorothy eventually defeated the Wicked Witch by throwing a bucket of water on her, causing her to melt. After rescuing her friends and using a magical Golden Cap to command the Winged Monkeys to fly them back to the Emerald City, Dorothy discovered that Oz was merely a humbug. Though Oz built a hot-air balloon to take her home, it accidentally departed without her. Seeking another way to return to Kansas, Dorothy and her companions journeyed south to ask for the assistance of Glinda, the Good Witch of the South. After surviving encounters in a fragile china country and overcoming the armless Hammer-Heads, they reached Glinda's castle. Glinda revealed that Dorothy's silver shoes possessed the magical ability to carry her anywhere.

unit: Dorothy, an orphan who lived with her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em on the dry gray prairies of Kansas, was swept away inside her farmhouse by a severe cyclone. She landed in the magical Land of Oz, inadvertently crushing the Wicked Witch of the East. Given the Witch's silver shoes by the Witch of the North and advised to seek help from the Great Wizard Oz, Dorothy set out along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City to find a way home. Along her journey, she befriended and recruited the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, facing numerous hazards including dangerous Kalidahs, a swift river, and a field of sleeping poppies before reaching their destination. Upon arriving at the Emerald City, the group met Oz, who demanded they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West before he would grant their wishes. Traveling to the West, they were attacked by the Witch's forces, and Dorothy was captured and enslaved in the Witch's castle. Dorothy eventually defeated the Wicked Witch by throwing a bucket of water on her, causing her to melt. After rescuing her friends and using a magical Golden Cap to command the Winged Monkeys to fly them back to the Emerald City, Dorothy discovered that Oz was merely a humbug. Though Oz built a hot-air balloon to take her home, it accidentally departed without her. Seeking another way to return to Kansas, Dorothy and her companions journeyed south to ask for the assistance of Glinda, the Good Witch of the South. After surviving encounters in a fragile china country and overcoming the armless Hammer-Heads, they reached Glinda's castle. Glinda revealed that Dorothy's silver shoes possessed the magical ability to carry her anywhere.

label: History
value: General Jinjur formerly made beds
unit: Formerly accustomed to making beds and washing dishes for her mother, General Jinjur led an Army of Revolt composed of young women to take over the Emerald City. Armed with knitting needles, her forces captured the city without bloodshed, forcing the Scarecrow to flee. Queen Jinjur later enlisted Mombi's magic to hinder her enemies and occupied the royal throne, though her army was briefly routed from the palace when the Scarecrow released mice. Ultimately, Glinda and Princess Ozma launched an aerial assault on the Emerald City to capture Jinjur after she refused to step down, effectively ending her revolt.

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: “There!” said she; “it is time for me to go. Carry that basket for me and help yourself to its contents if you are hungry.”

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: “Oh, no”, said Jinjur. “What man would oppose a girl, or dare to harm her? And there is not an ugly face in my entire Army.”

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: “To think,” she moaned, “that after having ruled as Queen, and lived in a palace, I must go back to scrubbing floors and churning butter again! It is too horrible to think of! I will never consent!”

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: "I have taken it, as you see; so just now I am the Queen, and all who oppose me are guilty of treason, and must be punished by the law you have just mentioned."

label: Quote
value: General Jinjur said: "The enemy is still outside the walls, so we must try to gain time by engaging them in parley. Go you with a flag of truce to Glinda and ask her why she has dared to invade my dominions, and what are her demands."

label: History
value: Glinda welcomed Dorothy and her companions to her castle in the South Country
unit: A beautiful, long-lived woman, Glinda welcomed Dorothy and her companions to her castle in the South Country and helped them by using the Golden Cap to send Dorothy's friends to their respective realms while explaining that Dorothy's Silver Shoes could carry her home. Later, when travelers sought her aid to liberate the Emerald City, Glinda determined from her records that Princess Ozma was the rightful ruler and had been hidden by the witch Mombi, prompting Glinda to march her army to the city. After seeing through Mombi's magical disguises, Glinda chased the fleeing witch across the desert on the Sawhorse, captured her, and used a truth-detecting pearl to force Mombi to confess that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip. Glinda then compelled Mombi to undo the spell, launched an aerial assault on the Emerald City to capture General Jinjur, and successfully restored Princess Ozma to the throne.

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City,” said Glinda, “for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler.”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: "yet I cannot understand how I have been defeated so easily by an old Witch who knows far less of magic than I do myself."

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “That is true,” replied the Sorceress, slowly. “But the Emerald City is now ruled by General Jinjur, who has caused herself to be proclaimed Queen. What right have I to oppose her?”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “Then,” decided Glinda, “I will march with my army to the Emerald City, and take Mombi prisoner. After that we can, perhaps, force her to tell the truth about Ozma.”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “I am quite obstinate myself,” returned the Sorceress, with a sweet smile. “so I do not fear Mombi in the least. Today I will make all necessary preparations, and we will march upon the Emerald City at daybreak tomorrow.”

label: History
value: The Great Oz is known to the inhabitants of the land as a powerful ruler.
unit: Known to the inhabitants of the land as a powerful ruler, the Great Oz requires visitors to the Emerald City to wear green-tinted spectacles before granting them individual audiences in his palace. When Dorothy and her companions seek his help, he assumes a different magical form for each visitor—appearing as a giant Head, a winged Lady, a five-eyed Beast, and a Ball of Fire—and refuses to fulfill their wishes until they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. Upon their return, Toto knocks over a screen in the throne room, exposing Oz as a non-magical ventriloquist and ordinary man from Omaha. After admitting he is a humbug who has been deceiving everyone, he promises to grant the group's requests the next day.

Upon their return, Toto knocks over a screen in the throne room, exposing Oz as a non-magical ventriloquist and ordinary man from Omaha. After admitting he is a humbug who has been deceiving everyone, he promises to grant the group's requests the next day.

value: Great Oz said: "I have fooled everyone so long that I thought I should never be found out. It was a great mistake my ever letting you into the Throne Room. Usually I will not see even my subjects, and so they believe I am something terrible."

label: History
value: Green Whiskers served as a Royal Army
unit: Green Whiskers previously served as a good Royal Army during the reign of the Wonderful Wizard. When Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse arrived at the Emerald City, Green Whiskers fitted them with green spectacles, escorted Jack to the Scarecrow, and later fetched Jellia Jamb to serve as an interpreter during their initial meeting. When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt attacked the city, the invaders discovered that Green Whiskers's gun was unloaded and quickly captured the Emerald City, prompting Green Whiskers to retreat to the palace to inform the Scarecrow.

label: History
value: The Guardian locked green-tinted spectacles onto Dorothy
unit: When Dorothy and her companions first arrived at the Emerald City, the Guardian locked green-tinted spectacles onto each traveler before leading them inside the gates. Later, when Dorothy's group departed for the South Country, they took their leave of him. He subsequently attached green spectacles to Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse upon their arrival at the city and escorted Jack to see the Scarecrow. Shortly after, when General Jinjur's Army of Revolt marched on the Emerald City, the female rebels quickly overpowered the Guardian at the city gates using knitting needles.

label: History
value: The Gump once was a monarch of the forest.
unit: Once a monarch of the forest with legs that carried him swiftly, the Gump was killed and his mounted head was later used by Nick Chopper and Tip to construct a flying creature, which Tip brought to life using the Powder of Life. After the Woggle-Bug repaired his broken wings with a wishing pill, the Gump flew Tip and his companions to pursue the disguised witch Mombi across the desert and transport her back to camp after Glinda captured her. He was then used to launch an aerial assault on the Emerald City to capture General Jinjur, after which he was dismantled upon his own request.

label: History
value: The wooden Saw-Horse was brought to life by Tip using Mombi's Powder of Life.
unit: Brought to life by Tip using Mombi's Powder of Life, the wooden Saw-Horse was fitted with carved wooden ears by Tip so it could hear and speak, and a post was hammered into its back as a handhold for Jack Pumpkinhead. Tip guided the horse along the yellow brick road, but when commanded to trot while crossing a river, the horse sped off too quickly, snapping off its tail and leaving Tip behind. It carried Jack into the Emerald City, where they were fitted with green spectacles and brought to the Scarecrow. Later, tied securely to Tip, Jack, and the Scarecrow, the Saw-Horse burst out of the palace gates to escape Jinjur's army, plunging into a wide river before carrying the companions onward to the Tin Woodman's palace. During their journey back to reclaim the throne, the Saw-Horse tripped in a rabbit hole and broke its leg. The injury was repaired after the newly recruited Woggle-Bug suggested replacing the broken leg with one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs. The party pressed on past magical illusions to reach the Emerald City, where they briefly took back the palace before fleeing to the roof to construct an animated flying Gump. After escaping the city aboard the Gump and crashing into a giant Jackdaw nest, the Saw-Horse figured out how to fulfill the counting requirement for Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, enabling the group to repair the Gump's wings and reach the palace of Glinda the Good.

unit: Brought to life by Tip using Mombi's Powder of Life, the wooden Saw-Horse was fitted with carved wooden ears by Tip so it could hear and speak, and a post was hammered into its back as a handhold for Jack Pumpkinhead. Tip guided the horse along the yellow brick road, but when commanded to trot while crossing a river, the horse sped off too quickly, snapping off its tail and leaving Tip behind. It carried Jack into the Emerald City, where they were fitted with green spectacles and brought to the Scarecrow. Later, tied securely to Tip, Jack, and the Scarecrow, the Saw-Horse burst out of the palace gates to escape Jinjur's army, plunging into a wide river before carrying the companions onward to the Tin Woodman's palace. During their journey back to reclaim the throne, the Saw-Horse tripped in a rabbit hole and broke its leg. The injury was repaired after the newly recruited Woggle-Bug suggested replacing the broken leg with one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs. The party pressed on past magical illusions to reach the Emerald City, where they briefly took back the palace before fleeing to the roof to construct an animated flying Gump. After escaping the city aboard the Gump and crashing into a giant Jackdaw nest, the Saw-Horse figured out how to fulfill the counting requirement for Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, enabling the group to repair the Gump's wings and reach the palace of Glinda the Good.

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Well, I cannot claim any great experience in life,” the Saw-Horse answered for himself. “but I seem to learn very quickly, and often it occurs to me that I know more than any of those around me.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Then it pleases me to be able to call you a fool, in return,” said the horse. “For I did not make the river, nor put it in our way; so only a term of, reproach is fit for one who becomes angry with me for falling into the water.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Then I will do as you tell me,” replied the Saw-Horse, humbly. “But what happened to me, a moment ago? I don’t seem to be just right, someway.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “I’m off, too!” cried the Saw-Horse, turning and prancing with agitation; “for my wood is so dry it would burn like kindlings.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “I’ll have nothing more to do with that Pumpkinhead,” declared the Saw-Horse, viciously. “he loses his head too easily to suit me.”

label: Jack Pumpkinhead
value: The Saw-Horse serves as a primary mode of transport for Jack Pumpkinhead.
unit: The Saw-Horse serves as a primary mode of transport for Jack Pumpkinhead and his companions after Tip fits the wooden horse with ears and a peg to hold onto. Jack relies on the Saw-Horse's swift movement to travel toward the Emerald City and escape later perils, though the horse's runaway speed at times leaves other party members behind. Throughout their journey, the two remain loyal traveling companions, sharing meals, rest, and repairs alongside the rest of their group.

label: History
value: Jack Pumpkinhead was constructed out of wood.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was constructed out of wood and a carved pumpkin by a boy named Tip, who intended to use him as a prank. Brought to life by the sorceress Mombi using the Powder of Life, Jack escaped into the night with Tip to travel to the Emerald City. Along the way, he rode a wooden sawhorse that Tip animated for him. Separated from Tip briefly, Jack entered the Emerald City and met the Scarecrow King, overcoming a language misunderstanding to become his friend. After Jinjur's Army of Revolt invaded, Jack escaped the city with Tip and the Scarecrow, eventually reuniting his pumpkin head with his body after a dip in the river. He visited the Tin Woodman's palace, where his wooden joint was repaired, and joined the group as they traveled across Oz. Along the journey, Jack surrendered one of his wooden legs to repair the Saw-Horse's broken limb, which was later replaced with a table leg by the Tin Woodman. He flew with his companions on the animated Gump, endured an attack by angry Jackdaws while protected beneath the Scarecrow's straw, and eventually reached the palace of Glinda the Good. Jack witnessed the surrender of Jinjur, the transformation of Tip back into Princess Ozma, and Ozma's subsequent coronation.

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “My name is Jack Pumpkinhead,” returned the other, smilingly; “but as to my business, I haven’t the least idea in the world what it is.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “It seems to me that I have,” replied the Pumpkinhead, seriously; “but I cannot think what it is. My father knows all about it, but he is not here.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “But I hope she cannot get at us,” exclaimed the Pumpkinhead, with a shiver of fear. “She threatened to make tarts of me, you know.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “Oh, dear!” moaned Jack; “what an unhappy lot is mine! Why, dear father, did you not make me out of tin—or even out of straw—so that I would keep indefinitely.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “First, however,” said the Pumpkinhead, “I beg you will release me from this horse, and make me another leg to walk with. For in my present condition I am of no use to myself or to anyone else.”

label: History
value: Mombi was an old sorceress
unit: Mombi was an old sorceress living in the Gillikin region of Oz who was taught magical tricks by the Wizard of Oz and obtained the Powder of Life from Nikidik. After returning home with new magic items, she used the powder to bring Tip's wooden creation, Jack Pumpkinhead, to life, but her plan to turn Tip into a marble statue caused the boy to steal her remaining powder and flee. She later aligned with General Jinjur to stop the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, conjuring magical illusions and confusing fields to impede their travel. When Glinda surrounded the Emerald City, Mombi attempted to evade capture through disguises and shape-shifting—including transforming into a rose, an ant, and a giant Griffin—before being pursued and caught in the desert. Under questioning with Glinda's truth-detecting pearl, Mombi confessed to having transformed the baby Princess Ozma into Tip, and she subsequently performed the incantation to break the spell and restore the princess to her true form.

label: History
value: Nick Chopper destroyed the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves.
unit: Nick Chopper, also known as the Tin Woodman, previously destroyed the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves and was invited to rule over the Winkies after her defeat. When his friends arrive at his palace seeking help against a rebellion in the Emerald City, he warmly greets them and agrees to join their journey to reclaim the throne. During their travels and subsequent siege in the royal palace, he helps construct a flying escape machine called the Gump using various household objects. While attending a meeting in Glinda's tent, a rose he wears is revealed to be the transformed witch Mombi, leading to a high-speed desert chase before Mombi is finally captured.

label: History
value: Princess Ozma was reared from childhood by Mombi.
unit: Reared from childhood by the old witch Mombi with no memory of her parents, Princess Ozma was hidden away as a baby after the Wizard left her in the witch's care. Mombi used a magical enchantment to transform the infant princess into the boy named Tip. After Glinda captured Mombi and forced her to reveal the truth under a magic pearl, Mombi performed an incantation that restored Ozma to her true form as a princess. Ozma then led an aerial assault alongside Glinda to remove General Jinjur, after which she was crowned Queen of the Emerald City and praised her loyal companions before they departed.

label: Appearance
value: The Scarecrow is a light-weight stuffed man.

He wears a worn and faded blue suit of clothes stuffed with straw, padded gloves, and old boots with blue tops. Atop his head sits a heavy golden crown set thick with sparkling jewels.

label: Personality
value: The Scarecrow is a happy character.
unit: The Scarecrow is a happy, contented, and thoughtful character who possesses a gay and charming demeanor, remaining remarkably calm under all circumstances. Lacking physical human needs, he does not require food, rest, or sleep, and he is able to see in the dark as effectively as by day. His primary early goal was to travel to the Emerald City and obtain brains from the Great Oz, desiring to become wise and be like other men, while also striving to help Dorothy return to Kansas. After achieving his wish for brains, he gained the reputation of being the wisest personage in the Land of Oz, taking pride in his education, philosophy, and wisdom. Following his appointment as ruler of the Emerald City, he works to defend his throne against the Army of Revolt, eager to save his friends and temporarily rule until Princess Ozma is found. Despite his composed nature, he harbors a deep fear of fire and lighted matches, which could ignite the straw inside him.

Upon reaching the Emerald City, Oz refused to grant their wishes until they destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West, prompting the group to journey west. Returning to the Emerald City, the travelers discovered Oz was an ordinary man, but he nevertheless fulfilled the Scarecrow's request by stuffing his head with bran and pins to serve as brains. label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: “I don’t know enough,” replied the Scarecrow cheerfully. “My head is stuffed with straw, you know, and that is why I am going to Oz to ask him for some brains.”

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: “All the same,” said the Scarecrow, “I shall ask for brains instead of a heart; for a fool would not know what to do with a heart if he had one.”

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: "and he would never hurt anyone who is our friend. If you will help us to save him I promise that he shall treat you all with kindness."

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: “I will return to the Emerald City,” he replied, “for Oz has made me its ruler and the people like me. The only thing that worries me is how to cross the hill of the Hammer-Heads.”

label: Quote
value: Scarecrow said: "How delighted I shall be to see my old friend the Tin Woodman again! I hope that he rules his people more successfully than I have ruled mine!"

value: The Queen of the Field Mice was rescued from a wildcat by the Tin Woodman.
unit: After being rescued from a wildcat by the Tin Woodman, the Queen of the Field Mice offered her gratitude and the help of her subjects to his companions. She gathered thousands of mice to pull a wooden cart, successfully hauling the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of a dangerous poppy field to safety. Later, she encountered the travelers again on their journey and lent twelve mice to hide in the Scarecrow's straw. She then guided the group past several of Mombi's magical illusions, leading them safely to the outside of the Emerald City.

label: Personality
value: The Tin Woodman is remarkably kind-hearted.
unit: The Tin Woodman is a remarkably kind-hearted, tender, and sensitive character who is entirely lacking in vanity. Driven by a deep desire to possess a heart, he seeks one from Oz so that he may love and marry a Munchkin maiden, valuing a good heart far above brains or education. He is always careful not to harm any living creature, weeping tears of sorrow if he accidentally causes injury and demonstrating a strong aversion to killing anyone. In addition to his primary quest, he is glad to be of use to Dorothy, helping her reach the Emerald City and get home. Beyond his gentle nature, he is a proud man who possesses a cheerful disposition and a fondness for flowers. He is also a skillful mechanic who aspires to return to the Country of the West to rule over the Winkies, of whom he is very fond.

label: History
value: Tin Woodman is the son of a woodman.
unit: Born the son of a woodman, the Tin Woodman grew up to become a wood-chopper and cared for his mother until her death. Originally made of flesh, he was transformed into tin after the Wicked Witch of the East cursed his axe, subsequently losing his heart and rusting motionless in the forest for a year. Upon being oiled and freed by Dorothy and the Scarecrow, he joined their journey along the yellow brick road to request a heart from the Great Oz. Along the way, he used his axe to build a raft, slay a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, and cut through aggressive trees, establishing a lasting friendship with the Mouse Queen. Though he was destroyed by Winged Monkeys sent by the Wicked Witch of the West, Winkie tinsmiths repaired him after the Witch's defeat, and he accepted an invitation from the Winkies to become their ruler. Returning to the Emerald City, he received a silk heart from Oz and later aided Dorothy on her journey south to Glinda the Good. He eventually joined the Scarecrow to liberate the Emerald City from General Jinjur's Revolt, surviving attacks in a giant Jackdaw nest, accepting a diamond necklace from the Woggle-Bug, and accidentally carrying Mombi transformed as a rose out of the city. Following Princess Ozma's restoration to the throne, he was commended for his virtue of heart before departing for the Winkie country.

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “Yes,” answered the tin man, “I did. I’ve been groaning for more than a year, and no one has ever heard me before or come to help me.”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “Get an oil-can and oil my joints,” he answered. “They are rusted so badly that I cannot move them at all; if I am well oiled I shall soon be all right again. You will find an oil-can on a shelf in my cottage.”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “This is a great comfort,” he said. “I have been holding that axe in the air ever since I rusted, and I’m glad to be able to put it down at last. Now, if you will oil the joints of my legs, I shall be all right once more.”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “I might have stood there always if you had not come along,” he said; “so you have certainly saved my life. How did you happen to be here?”

label: Quote
value: Tin Woodman said: “True,” the Tin Woodman returned. “So, if you will allow me to join your party, I will also go to the Emerald City and ask Oz to help me.”

label: History
value: Toto lived in Kansas.
unit: Toto originally lived in Kansas, where he loved to chase mice. He is carried away to the magical Land of Oz alongside Dorothy when a severe cyclone lifts their farmhouse into the air. Journeying along the yellow brick road, Toto travels with Dorothy and her new companions, though he succumbs to a magical sleeping spell in a poppy field before being carried to safety. Upon reaching the Emerald City and being sent to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, Toto is captured alongside Dorothy by the Winged Monkeys, but they are freed after Dorothy melts the Witch. After returning to the Emerald City, Toto inadvertently exposes the Great Oz as an ordinary humbug from Omaha by knocking over a screen in the Throne Room. Later, Toto runs off just as Oz's hot-air balloon is about to launch, causing Dorothy to miss her ride home. Following a journey to the South Country and an audience with Glinda the Good Witch, Toto returns safely to Kansas with Dorothy via the power of her Silver Shoes.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West spotted Dorothy and her companions traveling west.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West spotted Dorothy and her companions traveling west to find her and dispatched wolves, crows, bees, and Winkie soldiers to destroy them. When her initial attacks failed, she used the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and bring Dorothy to her castle as a servant. After attempting to starve the Lion, the Witch tricked Dorothy into losing one of her Silver Shoes, sparking an argument. In response, Dorothy threw a bucket of water on the Witch, causing her to completely melt away and freeing her captives.

label: History
value: The Wizard is originally from Omaha.
unit: Originally from Omaha, the Wizard once worked in a circus before arriving in the land of Oz floating in a runaway hot-air balloon. Upon descending from the clouds, local residents mistook him for a great wizard; he then usurped the throne from King Pastoria, ordered the construction of the Emerald City, and hid the infant Princess Ozma away with Mombi, whom he taught magic tricks. While ruling, he encountered the Winged Monkeys in the Land of the West, an experience he had no desire to repeat. Seeking to return to Kansas, he eventually constructed a new hot-air balloon alongside Dorothy, but when its ropes snapped as Dorothy chased her dog Toto, the balloon carried him away alone, leaving her behind.

label: v1 · Chapter I The Cyclone
value: Dorothy lives in an environment in Kansas.
chapter: v1 · Chapter I The Cyclone
unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. A sudden and severe cyclone strikes the farm, prompting Uncle Henry to tend to the livestock and Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. Delayed while retrieving Toto, Dorothy is trapped inside the small house as it is lifted high into the air by the storm, where she eventually relaxes and falls asleep as it floats away.

unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

value: General Jinjur summons Mombi.
chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

label: v1 · Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
value: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
unit: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft, but the swift current sweeps them off course and leaves the Scarecrow stuck on a pole. After the Lion swims the raft to shore, a friendly Stork flies over to rescue the Scarecrow. Continuing their journey through a field of deadly scarlet poppies, Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion succumb to the flowers' magical sleeping spell, forcing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to carry Dorothy and Toto to safety while leaving the heavy Lion behind.

value: The Tin Woodman slays a wildcat.
chapter: v1 · Chapter IX The Queen of the Field Mice
unit: The Tin Woodman slays a wildcat that is chasing the Queen of the Field Mice, earning her gratitude and the assistance of her subjects. The Scarecrow devises a plan for thousands of field mice to pull a wooden truck built by the Woodman to haul the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of the dangerous poppy field. Once the Lion is rescued to safety and Dorothy wakes up to thank them, the mice depart and the companions wait for the Lion to awaken.

value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

value: Dorothy and her companions travel through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft, but the swift current sweeps them off course and leaves the Scarecrow stuck on a pole. chapter: v1 · Chapter IX The Queen of the Field Mice
unit: The Tin Woodman slays a wildcat that is chasing the Queen of the Field Mice, earning her gratitude and the assistance of her subjects. value: Dorothy wakes up.

unit: Dorothy and the Scarecrow wake up and discover the Tin Woodman, rusted motionless in the forest. As they continue along the yellow brick road, the Tin Woodman recounts how the Wicked Witch of the East cursed his axe, leading to his tin transformation and loss of his heart.

label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

value: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VIII The Deadly Poppy Field
unit: The travelers attempt to cross the river on a raft, but the swift current sweeps them off course and leaves the Scarecrow stuck on a pole. After the Lion swims the raft to shore, a friendly Stork flies over to rescue the Scarecrow. Continuing their journey through a field of deadly scarlet poppies, Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion succumb to the flowers' magical sleeping spell, forcing the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to carry Dorothy and Toto to safety while leaving the heavy Lion behind.

value: Dorothy lives in Kansas.
chapter: v1 · Chapter I The Cyclone
unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. A sudden and severe cyclone strikes the farm, prompting Uncle Henry to tend to the livestock and Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. Delayed while retrieving Toto, Dorothy is trapped inside the small house as it is lifted high into the air by the storm, where she eventually relaxes and falls asleep as it floats away.

unit: Dorothy wakes up to find her house has landed safely in a beautiful land, inadvertently crushing the Wicked Witch of the East. unit: Dorothy and the Scarecrow wake up and discover the Tin Woodman, rusted motionless in the forest. label: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VI The Cowardly Lion
unit: While traveling through a thick forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion who attacks the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, then threatens Toto. Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose and calls him a coward, prompting the Lion to admit his secret lack of courage. He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

unit: Jack Pumpkinhead meets the Scarecrow King, but due to a misunderstanding, Jack believes they speak different languages. Tip commands the Saw-Horse to trot, but the horse speeds off too quickly, snapping its tail off in Tip's hands and leaving the boy behind. Jack and the Saw-Horse arrive at the Emerald City, where the Guardian of the Gates and the Soldier with the Green Whiskers put green spectacles on them and escort Jack to see the Scarecrow.

unit: Tip follows the Soldier to the palace, where the Scarecrow learns that the Emerald City is being conquered by an army of girls. unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. When the issue of the Saw-Horse's broken leg arises, the Woggle-Bug suggests using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs to fix it, allowing the party to resume their travel.

chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

chapter: v2 · In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. At dawn, realizing the Gump has flown them completely out of the Land of Oz, Tip orders a landing on a mountain cliff, which results in a crash into a giant Jackdaw nest where the group becomes trapped.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

unit: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi in disguise. Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

label: v2 · The Riches of Content
value: General Jinjur refuses to step down.
chapter: v2 · The Riches of Content
unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

chapter: v2 · A Highly Magnified History
unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. He accepts an invitation from Tip and the group to join them on their journey to the Emerald City. When the issue of the Saw-Horse's broken leg arises, the Woggle-Bug suggests using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs to fix it, allowing the party to resume their travel.

chapter: v2 · The Prisoners of the Queen
unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. Jinjur signals her Army of Revolt to ambush and disarm the group, threatening them with execution. The Scarecrow releases mice hidden in his straw, causing the female rebels and Jinjur to flee in panic, allowing the group to secure the palace doors.

unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. unit: In Glinda's tent, the Sorceress realizes the rose worn by Nick Chopper is actually Mombi in disguise. Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

Mombi repeatedly changes shape—from a shadow to an ant, then to a massive Griffin—and breaks free, prompting Glinda to chase her across the desert on the Sawhorse while Tip and the others follow in the Gump. Mombi eventually collapses from exhaustion in the sands, where Glinda uses a golden thread to undo the transformation and capture the old Witch.

unit: General Jinjur refuses to step down, prompting Glinda and Princess Ozma to launch an aerial assault using the Gump to enter the Emerald City and capture her. With the Revolt ended, Ozma is crowned Queen, restoring order to the kingdom and dismantling the Gump upon its own request. Before the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow depart for the Winkie country, Ozma commends them for their rich virtues of heart and brain.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

value: Dorothy and her companions encounter a roaring Lion while traveling through a thick forest.

He decides to join their journey to the Great Oz to request courage, and later in the day, the Scarecrow uses an oil-can to free the Tin Woodman's rusted jaws after the Woodman cries over accidentally stepping on a beetle.

unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Despite admitting he is a humbug without real magic, he promises to grant the group their requests the following day.

unit: Following Oz's departure, Dorothy gathers with her companions in the Throne Room to discuss how she can return to Kansas. She uses the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys, but the Monkey King explains they cannot cross the desert. After consulting with the soldier with green whiskers, the group learns about Glinda, the Good Witch of the South, and resolves to travel south together to seek her help.

unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. After accidentally startling a milkmaid and causing her cow to break a leg, they speak with a china princess and a cracked clown named Mr. Joker, who explain how fragile they are and why they cannot leave their land. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

label: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

Finally, the Witch uses the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys, who destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and carry Dorothy and Toto to the Witch's castle, where Dorothy is made a servant while secretly helping the imprisoned Lion.

label: v1 · Chapter XIII The Rescue
value: Dorothy frees the Cowardly Lion.
chapter: v1 · Chapter XIII The Rescue
unit: Dorothy frees the Cowardly Lion and informs the Winkies that they are no longer enslaved following the Wicked Witch's death. With the Winkies' assistance, Dorothy and the Lion retrieve the damaged Tin Woodman and the scattered clothes of the Scarecrow. Winkie tinsmiths repair the Tin Woodman, and the Scarecrow is re-stuffed with fresh straw. After a joyous reunion, the companions receive farewell gifts from the Winkies, and Dorothy claims the Golden Cap before they set out on their return journey to the Emerald City.

unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. chapter: v1 · Chapter XII The Search for the Wicked Witch
unit: Dorothy and her companions leave the Emerald City and travel west to find the Wicked Witch. The Witch spots them from her castle and sends wolves, crows, bees, and Winkie soldiers to destroy them, but Dorothy's friends defeat each wave. Finally, the Witch uses the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys, who destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and carry Dorothy and Toto to the Witch's castle, where Dorothy is made a servant while secretly helping the imprisoned Lion.

label: v1 · Chapter XIII The Rescue
value: Dorothy frees the Cowardly Lion.
chapter: v1 · Chapter XIII The Rescue
unit: Dorothy frees the Cowardly Lion and informs the Winkies that they are no longer enslaved following the Wicked Witch's death. With the Winkies' assistance, Dorothy and the Lion retrieve the damaged Tin Woodman and the scattered clothes of the Scarecrow. Winkie tinsmiths repair the Tin Woodman, and the Scarecrow is re-stuffed with fresh straw. After a joyous reunion, the companions receive farewell gifts from the Winkies, and Dorothy claims the Golden Cap before they set out on their return journey to the Emerald City.

section: Chapter II The Council with the Munchkins
label: Chapter II The Council with the Munchkins
value: Dorothy lives in an environment in Kansas.
chapter: Chapter II The Council with the Munchkins
unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. A sudden and severe cyclone strikes the farm, prompting Uncle Henry to tend to the livestock and Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. Delayed while retrieving Toto, Dorothy is trapped inside the small house as it is lifted high into the air by the storm, where she eventually relaxes and falls asleep as it floats away.

value: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder.
chapter: Chapter XXI The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts
unit: The group uses the Tin Woodman's ladder to climb over a mysterious wall into a country made entirely of china, complete with fragile china inhabitants. After accidentally startling a milkmaid and causing her cow to break a leg, they speak with a china princess and a cracked clown named Mr. Joker, who explain how fragile they are and why they cannot leave their land. Dorothy and her friends carefully journey through the china country to another wall, safely reaching the other side despite the Lion accidentally smashing a china church with his tail.

chapter: The Marvelous Powder of Life
unit: In the Gillikin region of Oz, a young boy named Tip lives under the care of the old sorceress Mombi, whom he dislikes. While Mombi is away on a two-day trip, Tip decides to construct a wooden figure with a carved pumpkin head to prank and frighten her. He completes the wooden dummy, dresses it in old clothes from Mombi's chest, and names his creation Jack Pumpkinhead.

unit: Tip positions Jack Pumpkinhead by the road to scare Mombi, who returns with new magical items obtained from a wizard. Finding the dummy, Mombi uses her new "Powder of Life" to bring Jack to life, catching Tip spying on her and bringing them all back to the house. That evening, Mombi brews a potion intended to transform Tip into a marble statue, locking the cooling potion in her room for the night while a terrified Tip sits by the fire.

unit: Fearing Mombi will turn him into a marble statue, Tip decides to run away and steals the Powder of Life and some food. chapter: Gen. Jinjur’s Army of Revolt
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead meets the Scarecrow King, but due to a misunderstanding, Jack believes they speak different languages. The Soldier with the Green Whiskers fetches Jellia Jamb to act as an interpreter, though she uses the opportunity to trick and tease both of them. Once Jellia reveals that everyone in Oz speaks the same language, the Scarecrow and Jack clear up the confusion and agree to become friends.

unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

unit: The Woggle-Bug explains his origin, how he gained education by listening to a schoolmaster, and how he became enlarged after being displayed on a magnifying screen. label: In the Jackdaw’s Nest
value: The group gathers various odd items on the roof.
chapter: In the Jackdaw’s Nest
unit: The group gathers various odd items on the roof to construct an escape flying machine. Led by Nick Chopper's assembly of sofas, palm leaves, ropes, a broom tail, and a mounted Gump head, Tip uses the remaining Powder of Life to bring the Gump creature to life. After a wild burst of flapping nearly blows them off the roof, Tip successfully commands the newly animated Gump to return and settle back down.

label: Dr. Nikidik’s Famous Wishing Pills
value: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip
chapter: Dr. Nikidik’s Famous Wishing Pills
unit: The newly revived Gump converses with Tip and his companions before flying them all south toward Glinda the Good. During the night flight, Tip discovers a hidden compartment in the pepper-box containing Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills, though the strange instructions leave them unsure how to use them. unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.
